newsitem.title: UK: UK music figures want Boosey to stay independent.
newsitem.headline: UK music figures want Boosey to stay independent.

text.p: Leading figures in the British classical music world have called for renowned instrument maker and music publisher Boosey & Hawkes Plc Plc to remain independent.

"We firmly believe it to be in the national interest that Boosey & Hawkes remains a single and independent firm," said a letter published in Wednesday's Times signed by a group including contemporary composers Harrison Birtwistle and James MacMillan.

The future of the company is uncertain after privately-owned U.S. music publisher Carl Fischer Inc put its 45 percent stake up for sale. Under British takeover rules any group acquiring the stake would have to make a full bid for the company.

"It seems most unlikely that a bidder would be competent, or would wish, to operate both the musical instrument and publishing arms. Therefore a takeover would inevitably lead to the break-up of the company," the letter added.
This would cause "irremediable damage" to Britain's musical heritage and harm the musical education of the young, many of whom use Boosey & Hawkes instruments and materials, the letter added.

It was also signed by administrators of the estates of composers Benjamin Britten, Edward Elgar, Igor Stravinsky and Sergei Prokofiev. The works of all four are part of the company's outstanding catalogue.
